judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short identifying preamble; the only oddity is 'by and among' used for exactly two parties, which changes nothing operative. No term here is capable of two reasonable readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fixes the Parties as only Licensee and Clearwire, yet Article V has Licensee representing to 'Clearwire and Clearwire Parent' and Section 7.02 imposes duties on Clearwire Parent, a non-signatory. That is a real, if minor, whole-instrument friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'bundle of value ... Total Consideration' recital is impressionistic and uses a but-for formulation ('would not have been executed but for all of the elements') whose legal effect is uncertain; 'EBS Economic Royalties' does not match the operative label 'Economic Royalties'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recitals frame the deal as an enduring exchange of access for a bundle of consideration, while operative Sections 2.02 and 9.01 make the $23M fully refundable on an 18-month expiry — a classic recital-versus-operative pull.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Essentially definitional, creating 'EBS Spectrum Capacity' by reference to Schedule A and the IUAs; the parenthetical 'when under IUA hereunder' is compressed but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Sections 1.02(a)-(b) and 4.02; nothing in Articles II or IX contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says the initial payment 'exceeds the value of the Initial Spectrum Capacity' and 'includes additional consideration for the Option and the ROFR' without quantifying any of the three components, so what part is earned and non-refundable is left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This sits directly against Section 2.02, which requires refund of the whole unapplied Prepaid Royalties Balance, and Section 2.01, which treats the entire $23M as prepaid royalties applicable only to IUAs; if part was consideration for the Option/ROFR it cannot also be wholly refundable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of Access Right Royalty components is introduced by 'among other items' and closed by 'together with technology, facilities, equipment and other functionality', a general catch-all against enumerated specifics whose reach is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is broadly consistent with Article III, but Article III contains no free-standing 'technology, facilities, equipment' obligation, so the overview promises slightly more than the operative article delivers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A summary provision defining 'Access Right Royalties' as the Article III bundle; the OCR-mangled words are cosmetic and the sense is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recitals call the same bundle plus the Economic Royalties the 'Total Consideration', and Section 1.01(c) labels the Article III items differently, but these can be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Option is exercisable only at a price 'to be negotiated in good faith based on the fair market value', i.e. an agreement to agree with only a cap; 'Available' and the trigger 'becomes Available' are load-bearing but defined only in an absent Exhibit I.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with Section 2.02's proviso that the Term is not deemed expired while 'the Option periods described in Section 1.02(b) have not terminated' and with Section 1.02(d)'s automatic lapse on expiry of the Term — a circle that has to be construed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It contains outright mechanical errors ('a GSA the covers the same metropolitan are in Puerto Rico') and the defined trigger 'Substantially Similar' is left vague, while the price floor of $0.10 sits against a $0.15 cap and a 'Higher Price' mechanic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Section 1.02(d)'s twelve-month Puerto Rico survival and Section 9.01's cryptic carve-out 'except as it pertains to Puerto Rico', neither of which states the same period cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence 'Any outstanding Options shall lapse automatically upon the expiration of the Term' is clear on its face, though the twelve-month PR carve-out 'without regard to the earlier expiration of the Term' is awkwardly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts Section 2.02 (Term not deemed expired while Option periods are open) and Section 9.03 (Option rights survive expiration or termination) — three provisions giving three different answers about Options after the Term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward covenant to cause Service Affiliates to assume and be jointly liable, with an express saving that Clearwire's primary obligation is not limited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Section 1.01(a)'s reference to Collateral Documents and Article III's Clearwire obligations; no other provision cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully sequenced; the softest points are 'bona fide written offer', 'comparable non-cash consideration' and the garbled 'for such timing remaining in the ROFR Period'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers disputes to 'arbitration under this Agreement' while Section 10.11 (the Dispute Resolution Procedure) is the only such mechanism and is incomplete in this instrument; it also interacts with Section 9.03's survival of ROFR rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative words — $23,000,000 payable on execution, defined as 'Prepaid Royalties' — are as definite as a payment term gets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Prepaid Royalties 'shall be applied as provided in Section 1.02(b)' against IUAs for both Initial and Future Spectrum Capacity, but Section 1.02(b) addresses only Future Spectrum Capacity, and Section 1.01(b) says part of the same payment bought the Option and ROFR; Section 2.02 then makes the unapplied balance refundable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso that 'the Term shall not be deemed to have expired for this purpose during a period that the Option periods described in Section 1.02(b) have not terminated' is self-referential and its trigger indeterminate, and Clearwire's unilateral right to extend the refund date is unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be squared with Section 9.01 (Term ends at the earlier of three events, one of which is the return of the money) or Section 1.02(d) (Options lapse on expiry of the Term): each provision makes the other's trigger depend on itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Commercially reasonable best efforts' to 'consider' entering a joint venture is an internally contradictory and unmeasurable standard, and the benchmark 'in a manner consistent with the way the Access Right Royalties are provided ... to third parties' has no ascertainable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Article III generally, though the closing condition about buying 'at greater than Clearwire's lowest wholesale price' pulls against Section 3.05(a)'s promise of the lowest wholesale rate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence signpost conferring entitlement 'as provided in' three named sections; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Sections 3.02(b), 3.03 and 3.04 exactly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The same capacity and characteristics as the highest level of premium mass market retail service' and 'without charge or expense' are benchmarks that shift with Clearwire's own offerings and could be read broadly or narrowly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is subordinated to Clearwire's 'then generally applicable Acceptable Use Policy', a document outside the Agreement, which sits uneasily with Section 10.03's entire-agreement clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Clearwire may not use the Educational Reservation' and the 5% reservation are definite; 'in such locations served by the Clearwire National Platform ... as Licensee desires' is broad but intelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It routes disagreements to 'the Dispute Resolution Procedure' in Section 10.11, which in this instrument is truncated, and the FCC-compliance duty overlaps Section 7.05.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The upward adjustment 'every five years proportionate to the growth of the overall data capacity ... as measured by its average throughput' leaves both the metric and the proportionality open, expressly conceding the Parties may not agree.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The five-year adjustment cycle here sits against Section 3.04(a)'s annual January 31 recalculation of the other class of Cost-Free Educational Accounts, and both are labelled 'Cost-Free Educational Accounts'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short bridging sentence ('in addition to, and not in lieu of') that defers all substance to Section 3.04(a).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It describes the Section 3.03 accounts as provided 'pursuant to the Educational Reservation', but Section 3.03(b)'s Basic accounts are a separate Clearwire deliverable rather than the Licensee's own 5% reservation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'greater of (X) two per Sector and (Y) the Formula Quantity' test is mechanical; 'Sector' and 'Market Area' are defined only in the absent Exhibit I.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The annual January 31 recalculation runs alongside Section 3.03(b)'s five-year adjustment and Section 3.04(b)'s launch-based delivery trigger, which do not obviously coordinate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subparagraph is mislabelled '(3)' where the following one is '(ii)', and 'rounded up or down to the nearest whole number' gives no rule for a .5 result; the Local Channel Ratio itself is defined precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.08(b) cross-refers to 'Sections 3.04(a)(ii)', so the mislabelling here makes the internal numbering of Section 3.04(a) uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Officially associated with such Educational End User' and 'outside of its Educational End User environment' are boundary phrases of uncertain reach, only partly cured by the university example.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly carved out of the resale prohibition in Section 3.08(b) and coordinates with Section 3.05; no conflict emerges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A delivery trigger keyed to commercial launch or the Commencement Date, whichever is later; plain enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Commencement Date' is an IUA term not defined in this instrument, which also affects Sections 3.01 and 3.07, but the usage is consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The lowest wholesale rate provided by Clearwire to an arms-length third party in such Market Area or other comparable market' turns on 'comparable market', an undefined and contestable benchmark.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.01's Puerto Rico joint-venture sentence contemplates purchases 'at greater than Clearwire's lowest wholesale price', which cuts against the most-favoured pricing promised here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A standard Clearwire wholesale agreement form drafted in a manner consistent with the terms of this Agreement' is an agreement to agree on a form not attached, and 'any Licensee' is odd where there is one Licensee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Incorporating an unattached Clearwire form sits awkwardly with Section 10.03's entire-agreement and written-amendment requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single priced obligation — end-user equipment at 10% above Clearwire's acquisition cost, for Educational End Users only — with a clear restriction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The no-resale limit tracks Sections 3.04(a)(ii) and 3.08(b); nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonably necessary support ... as contemplated by their agreement' has an unanchored referent ('their agreement'), and 'generally provided to Clearwire's retail customers or wholesalers to mass market customers' is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Section 3.08(a)'s Preferred Content Provider access rights and is qualified by Section 3.08(c)'s capacity-constraint reservation, but the two can be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The benchmark is 'the same degree of access to, and use of, any system capability ... provided to premium third party content providers', a comparator class Clearwire alone defines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is cut back by Section 3.08(c) and overlaps Section 3.07; those fit together without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Clearwire's most favored program suppliers' and 'equal features and/or service sets' are comparative standards with no stated method of comparison.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The resale ban is expressly reconciled with Sections 3.04(a)(ii) and 3.05, so the carve-outs line up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reservation of a right to restrict access when use 'is no longer commercially and technically feasible due to limitations in network capabilities' is a broad, self-judged escape from the Preferred Content Provider promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs Clearwire to 'comply with the provisions of ARTICLE III to ensure timely access to information about capacity usage', but Article III contains no information-access provision at all — a cross-reference that leads nowhere, and it partially guts Section 3.08(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Commercially reasonable best efforts' to secure carriage of 'one ordinary unpaid channel' on a third party's 'basic tier' is an unmeasurable duty over a matter outside Clearwire's control.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limited Reciprocity is listed in Section 1.01(c) as a core element of the Access Right Royalties, yet here it is only a best-efforts hope with costs passed to Licensee — a mismatch of framing but not a hard conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure signpost to subsections (a) through (c); 'required of it' is grammatically loose but harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Sections 4.01(a)-(c) and Section 4.02(a)'s Initial Closing on the Effective Date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An itemised delivery list; 'each a Wire Account' is plural language for a single account and 'Absent notice of different instructions' is undefined as to form, but the sense is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It brings in the Stock Pledge Agreement (Exhibit III) and Schedule 4.01, neither in this instrument, and the pledge presumably secures the Section 2.02 refund obligation that is the heart of the deal.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The delivery of 'the Upfront Royalty provided for in the applicable EBS Spectrum Capacity IUA as reflected on Schedule A' uses a term this Agreement never defines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.01 requires payment of $23,000,000 in 'Prepaid Royalties' on execution, and how the 'Upfront Royalty' relates to that sum — part of it, or additional — is not stated anywhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closing-certificate mechanic with two enumerated deliverables; nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is repeated consistently in Section 4.02(c)(ii)(2) and (iii)(2).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixes the Initial Closing on the Effective Date; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The table of contents numbers this section 4.03, a numbering slip, but the substance matches Sections 4.01 and 4.03 and Section 10.05 denies headings any effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsequent Closings happen 'as specified in the applicable IUAs when the Parties reach agreement on the pricing', which leaves closing dependent on a future agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That dependence links back to Section 1.02(b)'s good-faith price negotiation and Section 2.02's refund proviso; the three together make the end of the Term hard to fix.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'No Injunctions or Restraints' condition is a sentence fragment with no verb — it never says the order must not be 'in effect' — so the condition's operation must be supplied by inference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the only mutual closing condition and does not collide with Sections 4.02(c)(ii) or (iii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditions keyed to the IUA's representations being 'true and correct in all material respects' and to certified officer copies; standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Section 4.02(c)(iii) and does not disturb Article V or VI.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subsection is mislabelled '(ii)' although it follows another '(ii)', and it requires resolutions of 'each Clearwire Affiliate that is a Party hereto' when no Affiliate signs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble names only two Parties, so the reference to Clearwire Affiliates as Parties has no counterpart anywhere in the instrument except the Section 1.03 Service Affiliate concept.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence says all Closings occur electronically 'provided that the Initial Closing shall take place at the offices of Davis Wright Tremaine' — the proviso contradicts the rule within the same sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere fixes a closing venue, so the tension is internal to this provision rather than instrument-wide.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable best efforts ... all things necessary, proper or advisable' is boilerplate whose 'advisable' catch-all is broad but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside Sections 7.01 and 7.07, which use 'commercially reasonable efforts' and 'commercially reasonable best efforts' for overlapping duties — differing standards for similar obligations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard organisation and good standing representation with a Material Adverse Effect carve-out; the terms are conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Licensee Material Adverse Effect' is defined only in the absent Exhibit I but is used consistently across Article V and Section 8.02.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate authorisation and enforceability language with the usual bankruptcy and equity exceptions; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines 'Transactions' and 'Licensee Documents' in a way Sections 5.03, 8.01 and 10.01 then use consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional three-limb no-conflict representation; the enumerated instruments ('note, bond, mortgage, indenture, license, agreement or other obligation') end in a catch-all but that is standard usage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is subject to Schedule 5.03, which is not in the instrument, but its structure mirrors Section 6.03(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The whole representation is undone by the closing catch-all 'except as contemplated herein or therein', which has no ascertainable boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clearwire's parallel Section 6.03(b) expressly reserves the required FCC spectrum lease filings, while Licensee's version does not — the same regulatory fact is treated inconsistently across the two representation articles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Nor ... does there exist any basis therefore' misuses 'therefore' for 'therefor', and the carve-out for 'immaterial claims brought against Licensee in the ordinary course of business' is a vague and unusual exception to a litigation representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clearwire's Section 6.04 uses a different structure and qualifier, but the asymmetry is a bargained difference rather than an incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening stack — 'Excepting the markets listed on Schedule 5.05 and only to the best knowledge of the Licensee, assuming compliance ... by other parties to a Third Party Agreement' — layers four qualifiers before the representation, and 'complied in all respects' is then contradicted by a materiality carve-out in the same clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.02 strips out knowledge and materiality qualifiers when measuring Damages, which largely negates the qualifiers this representation was drafted to obtain; Section 5.07 then redefines 'best knowledge' more broadly still.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat, unqualified brokers representation; there is nothing to read two ways.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Section 6.06 exactly and no indemnity or fee provision cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines 'best knowledge' to include constructive knowledge 'after commercially reasonable investigation', a standard that is circular and expands rather than fixes the term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.04 uses plain 'knowledge' rather than 'best knowledge', so this definition leaves the litigation representation's standard unsettled, and Section 8.02 disregards knowledge qualifiers altogether for Damages.
